Accessibility: Skip TopNav Cosmetics Market to Reach USD 802.04 Billion by 2035 as Skincare, Fragrance and Online Beauty Drive Growth and Mega-Deals Reshape the Industry Skincare Holds About 40%, North America 34% and L'Oréal About 10–11% of a USD 450.20 Billion Market: Precedence Research Segment, Company and Buyer Intelligence November 17, 2026 10:37 ET | Source: Precedence Research Precedence Research Ottawa, Nov.  17, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The global cosmetics market is valued at USD 450.20 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 802.04 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of 6.56%. The U.S. market is set to grow from USD 107.98 billion in 2026 to USD sss195.66 billion by 2035, while fragrance and online sales are the fastest-growing parts of the industry. Precedence Research today released updated intelligence on the global cosmetics market, covering skincare, hair care, color cosmetics, fragrance and toiletries sold through mass, masstige and prestige channels . The market is valued at USD 450.20 billion in 2026 and is forecast to reach USD 802.04 billion by 2035, adding USD 351.84 billion in annual sales. Demand is steady, but the mix is shifting. Skincare remains the largest category at about 40% of sales , fragrance is the fastest-growing major category at about 8.5% a year, and online channels already account for about 26% of sales. Company results confirm the trend: L'Oréal's sales reached EUR 35.33 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 6.9% like-for-like with growth in every division and region, and Estée Lauder returned to growth with organic sales up 6% and fragrance up 20% in its latest quarter. The industry is also consolidating. Kimberly-Clark's USD 48.7 billion acquisition of Kenvue won shareholder approval in January 2026, Estée Lauder and Puig held talks on a combination valued at about USD 40 billion before ending them in May 2026, and L'Oréal has taken over Kering Beauté. For brand owners, retailers, ingredient and packaging suppliers and investors, the key questions are which categories and channels will grow fastest, and who will win scale in a market where the top 25 companies hold only about 55% of sales. Mass products still account for about 60% of value, but prestige brands, at about 28%, capture a larger share of profits. Skincare leads because of daily-use routines, dermo-cosmetics and sun protection . Fragrance grows fastest as consumers trade up to prestige and niche perfumes, a trend reflected in Estée Lauder's 20% fragrance growth and L'Oréal's move into luxury fragrance through Kering Beauté. Channel and consumer. Supermarkets and hypermarkets remain the largest channel, but online grows about 11% a year as social commerce and brand websites expand. Male grooming and vegan cosmetics and other clean products are growing faster than the market. The U.S. is the largest single market, at USD 107.98 billion in 2026. Estée Lauder reported continued North America growth in its latest quarter, and prestige fragrance and clinical skincare are the main drivers. Asia Pacific. Asia Pacific is a major growth engine. Estée Lauder's Asia/Pacific organic sales rose 10% in its latest quarter, helped by travel retail at Beijing and Shanghai airports and online sales in Hainan, and L'Oréal reported accelerating growth in India. Europe and Middle East & Africa. Europe is the industry's production and export hub, with about 40% of global export value. The Middle East & Africa is the fastest-growing region , led by Gulf luxury demand and halal cosmetics ; L'Oréal's SAPMENA-SSA zone led its regional growth in 2026. Sources: Expert Interview, Secondary Sources, Precedence Research Database, Precedence Research Analysts and Researcher What Is Changing in the Industry Figure 2: Beauty Leaders, Latest Results and Deals Sources: Expert Interview, Secondary Sources, Precedence Research Database, Precedence Research Analysts and Researcher Consolidation has reached record size. Kimberly-Clark's USD 48.7 billion acquisition of Kenvue, owner of Neutrogena and Aveeno, won shareholder approval in January 2026. Estée Lauder and Puig confirmed talks in March 2026 on a combination valued at about USD 40 billion, but the talks ended in May. What it indicates: Scale matters more as brands fight for retail space, media and supply chains, and large deals will keep returning. The leaders are buying into luxury fragrance. L'Oréal acquired Kering Beauté, including Creed and long-term licences for Kering's fashion houses, for about EUR 4 billion. What it indicates: Fragrance, the fastest-growing major category, is now a central battleground for the largest companies. Growth has returned for the prestige leaders. L'Oréal's nine-month 2026 sales grew 6.9% like-for-like with a strong recovery in its Luxe division, and Estée Lauder raised its fiscal 2027 outlook after organic growth of 6% and a jump in operating margin to 12.1%. What it indicates: The prestige segment is recovering after a difficult period, especially in Asia travel retail. Portfolios are being reshaped. Estée Lauder is selling Too Faced, Smashbox and Dr. Jart+, while e.l.f. Beauty agreed to buy Rhode for up to USD 1 billion and Unilever added wellness brands. What it indicates: Companies are focusing on fewer, faster-growing brands in skincare, fragrance and wellness. Premiumization in fragrance and prestige beauty. Growth of e-commerce and social commerce. Rising demand in India, the Middle East and Africa. Interest in natural, clean, vegan cosmetics and halal cosmetics . Raw material, packaging and logistics cost pressure. Regulatory change on ingredients and labeling. Volatile travel retail and luxury demand in China. Counterfeit products in online channels. Sustainable packaging and refillable formats as brands meet environmental goals. Consolidation has reached record size. Kimberly-Clark's USD 48.7 billion acquisition of Kenvue, owner of Neutrogena and Aveeno, won shareholder approval in January 2026. Estée Lauder and Puig confirmed talks in March 2026 on a combination valued at about USD 40 billion, but the talks ended in May.

What it indicates:
The leaders are buying into luxury fragrance. L'Oréal acquired Kering Beauté, including Creed and long-term licences for Kering's fashion houses, for about EUR 4 billion.
The leaders are buying into luxury fragrance.
What it indicates: Fragrance, the fastest-growing major category, is now a central battleground for the largest companies.
Growth has returned for the prestige leaders. L'Oréal's nine-month 2026 sales grew 6.9% like-for-like with a strong recovery in its Luxe division, and Estée Lauder raised its fiscal 2027 outlook after organic growth of 6% and a jump in operating margin to 12.1%.
Growth has returned for the prestige leaders.
What it indicates: The prestige segment is recovering after a difficult period, especially in Asia travel retail.
Portfolios are being reshaped. Estée Lauder is selling Too Faced, Smashbox and Dr. Jart+, while e.l.f. Beauty agreed to buy Rhode for up to USD 1 billion and Unilever added wellness brands.

articles.title: Adagene and City of Hope Open Clinical Trial to Test New Therapy for Patients with Hard-to-Treat Colorectal Cancer
articles.text:
Accessibility: Skip TopNav Adagene Announces Completion of Enrollment in Randomized Dose Optimization Phase 2 Trial of Muzastotug in Combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) in Microsatellite Stable Colorectal Cancer November 09, 2026 07:00 ET | Source: Adagene Inc. Adagene Inc. - Enrollment of 60 patients complete; initial results expected in 1H 2027 to inform dose regimen for the Phase 3 trial - Adagene continues to own worldwide commercial rights to muzastotug SAN DIEGO and SUZHOU, China, Nov.  09, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Adagene Inc. (Nasdaq: ADAG), a platform-driven, clinical-stage biotechnology company transforming the discovery and development of novel antibody-based therapies, today announced completion of enrollment in its randomized Phase 2 dose-optimization trial of muzastotug (ADG126), a masked, anti-CTLA-4 SAFEbody ® , in combination with Merck’s (known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada) anti-PD-1 therapy, KEYTRUDA ® (pembrolizumab), in patients with late-line microsatellite stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC) without liver metastases. “Completing enrollment in this randomized trial is an important step toward identifying the dose regimen of muzastotug for the Phase 3 registration trial,” said Peter Luo, Ph.D., Chairman and President of R&D at Adagene. “We acknowledge Sanofi’s additional equity investment associated with this trial, which supports continued development of muzastotug in solid tumors, including MSS CRC, where dose-limiting challenges have restricted the use of anti-CTLA-4 therapies. As we look ahead to initial results in the first half of 2027, we hope new data will validate muzastotug’s broad applicability and combinability, further enhanced by its induction and maintenance dosing regimens. This could position muzastotug as a transformative next-generation backbone for combination therapies across multiple indications, in both early- and late-line treatment settings. It could also unlock value in indications where legacy CTLA-4/PD-1 based combinations are already FDA-approved, as well as in historically refractory tumors like MSS CRC.” About the Phase 2 Trial The randomized Phase 2 trial (NCT05405595) was incorporated into the existing protocol for the Phase 1b/2 study following a 2025 meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The primary endpoint of the Phase 2 trial is overall response rate (ORR), and secondary endpoints include duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). The study enrolled 60 patients, randomized 1:1 into one of two treatment arms evaluating different dose regimens of muzastotug in combination with pembrolizumab. Both arms use induction to rapidly establish activated muzastotug exposure in tumors, followed by maintenance to sustain exposure and potentially improve ORR and OS: Arm A: Muzastotug 10 mg/kg every three weeks (Q3W) for four doses, followed by 10 mg/kg every six weeks (Q6W) maintenance Arm B: Muzastotug 20 mg/kg Q6W for two doses, followed by 15 mg/kg Q6W maintenance As previously announced in July 2025, the following elements of the Phase 3 trial design were also confirmed following a meeting with the FDA: Patient Population: Trials will enroll late-line patients with MSS CRC without liver metastases, including those with peritoneal metastasis/involvement. Phase 3 Trial Design: The FDA agreed with Adagene’s proposed standard-of-care (SOC) control arm for the Phase 3 clinical trial and confirmed that a muzastotug monotherapy arm was not required. Phase 3 Endpoints: The primary endpoint of the Phase 3 trial will be OS. Secondary endpoints will include PFS, DOR and ORR. About Adagene Adagene Inc. (Nasdaq: ADAG) is a platform-driven, clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to transforming the discovery and development of novel antibody-based cancer immunotherapies. Adagene combines computational biology and artificial intelligence to design novel antibodies that address globally unmet patient needs. The company has forged strategic collaborations with reputable global partners that leverage its SAFEbody ® precision masking technology in multiple approaches at the vanguard of science. Powered by its proprietary Dynamic Precision Library (DPL) platform, composed of NEObody™, SAFEbody, and POWERbody™ technologies, Adagene’s highly differentiated pipeline features novel immunotherapy programs. The company’s SAFEbody technology is designed to address safety and tolerability challenges associated with many antibody therapeutics by using precision masking technology to shield the binding domain of the biologic therapy. Through activation in the tumor microenvironment, this allows for tumor-specific targeting of antibodies, while minimizing on-target off-tumor toxicity in healthy tissues. Adagene’s lead clinical program, muzastotug (ADG126), is a masked, anti-CTLA-4 SAFEbody with FDA Fast Track designation that targets a unique epitope of CTLA-4 in regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the tumor microenvironment. Muzastotug is currently in Phase 1b/2 and Phase 2 clinical studies in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, particularly focused on microsatellite stable (MSS) metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC). Validated by ongoing clinical research, the SAFEbody platform can be applied to a wide variety of antibody-based therapeutic modalities, including Fc empowered antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and bi/multi-specific T-cell engagers. For more information, please visit: https://investor.adagene.com/ Follow Adagene on WeChat , LinkedIn and X . Accessibility: Skip TopNav POTS Phase 2 Trial Shows Baloncibart, a First-in-Class NPR1 Blocking Antibody, Reduced Orthostatic Heart Rate and Improved Orthostatic Symptoms November 12, 2026 17:00 ET | Source: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Data presented today for the first time at the American Autonomic Society (AAS) annual meeting POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) is a debilitating condition characterized by a marked increase in heart rate upon standing and associated orthostatic symptoms, with no FDA-approved treatments available A single dose of baloncibart reduced the exaggerated heart rate response to standing and improved orthostatic symptoms through four weeks; biomarker changes were consistent with plasma volume expansion, the intended effect of NPR1 blockade Potentially pivotal Phase 3 trial planned for first half of 2027 TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov.  12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced results from the Phase 2 PINNACLE trial in adults with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) evaluating baloncibart, a novel, investigational, first-in-class monoclonal antibody that blocks natriuretic peptide receptor 1 (NPR1). The data were presented for the first time at the American Autonomic Society’s (AAS) 37th International Symposium on the Autonomic Nervous System in San Diego, CA. POTS is a chronic disorder in which heart rate rises abnormally upon standing. Patients may experience palpitations, dizziness, fatigue, exercise intolerance, cognitive difficulties, gastrointestinal symptoms and chronic pain. Although historically underdiagnosed, recent estimates suggest it affects between 500,000 and several million people in the U.S., and the vast majority are young women. While the cause of POTS is unknown, it is believed to be associated with low blood volume. Baloncibart is designed to increase the volume of blood in circulation in an effort to reduce the increase in heart rate and symptoms that occur in people with POTS. “POTS causes debilitating symptoms that can profoundly disrupt daily life, and patients have no FDA-approved treatment options. In the trial, a single injection of baloncibart 450 mg reduced the exaggerated heart rate response to standing and improved orthostatic symptoms through four weeks,” said Satish R. Raj, M.D., Professor of Cardiac Science at the University of Calgary’s Cumming School of Medicine, and investigator in the trial. “The results are consistent with the rationale for NPR1 blockade in POTS, with biomarker changes pointing to an increase in blood volume alongside lower heart rate and better symptoms.” The randomized, double-blind, Phase 2 PINNACLE trial evaluated a single subcutaneous dose of baloncibart 150 mg (n=27) or 450 mg (n=28) compared to placebo (n=27) in patients with POTS. The primary endpoint was the change in heart rate from lying down to standing (DeltaHR) at day 8; no formal hypothesis testing was prespecified. Improvements were observed with baloncibart on DeltaHR and other key measures of the disease (i.e., symptoms and function) as assessed by the Living With POTS Questionnaire (LWPQ). The LWPQ is a novel patient-reported outcome tool to assess POTS symptoms and function in clinical trials, which is being developed by Regeneron in accordance with the FDA patient-focused drug development guidance. Baloncibart 450 mg reduced DeltaHR versus placebo at day 8 (primary endpoint) with a least-squares (LS) mean difference of -11.4 beats per minute (bpm; nominal p=0.0007), and at day 29 (secondary endpoint) with an LS mean difference of -7.4 bpm (nominal p=0.0124). Baloncibart 150 mg reduced DeltaHR versus placebo at day 8 (LS mean difference: -9.5 bpm; nominal p=0.0045), but the effect was not maintained at day 29. Baloncibart 450 mg improved orthostatic symptoms, physical functioning, and activities of daily living versus placebo at day 29, as measured by the LWPQ. Domain scores range from 0 to 100, with lower scores indicating fewer symptoms or less impairment. The LS mean differences in change from baseline for each domain were as follows: Orthostatic symptoms (baseline mean: 45.5): -12.9 points (nominal p=0.0096) Physical functioning (baseline mean: 55.1): -13.8 points (nominal p=0.0073) Activities of daily living (baseline mean: 48.7): -8.7 points (nominal p=0.1035) Overall across the three domains, there was no obvious improvement with baloncibart 150 mg compared to placebo Additionally at day 8, both doses of baloncibart led to changes in biomarkers consistent with the anticipated beneficial plasma volume expansion driven by NPR1 blockade, including an increase in NT-proBNP and reductions in standing norepinephrine and hemoglobin. Average standing systolic blood pressure increased for both doses, with observed mean changes from baseline at day 29 of 8.7 mmHg to a mean of 118.8 mmHg for baloncibart 450 mg and 5.4 mmHg to a mean of 114.0 mmHg for baloncibart 150 mg. In the trial, single doses of baloncibart up to 450 mg were generally well tolerated. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were mostly mild or moderate and occurred in 13 patients (48.1%) receiving placebo, 18 patients (66.7%) receiving baloncibart 150 mg, and 19 (67.9%) receiving baloncibart 450 mg; one severe TEAE occurred in the trial in the placebo group. TEAEs that occurred in ≥10% of patients in any treatment group, including placebo, baloncibart 150 mg and baloncibart 450 mg, were: injection site reaction (14.8%, 3.7%, and 17.9%), headache (0%, 11.1%, and 10.7%), syncope (11.1%, 14.8%, and 3.6%), heavy menstrual bleeding (0%, 11.1%, and 0%), and nasopharyngitis (11.1%, 0%, and 0%). Two serious TEAEs were reported: one case of headache with baloncibart 150 mg and one case of syncope with baloncibart 450 mg. No TEAE led to discontinuation. “POTS is a condition that disproportionately impacts younger women and has been under-recognized and under-served for too long, which is why it was critical to incorporate the patient experience in our trial design and measure symptoms that reflect how patients actually feel and function,” said Boaz Hirshberg, M.D., Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, Internal Medicine at Regeneron. “These initial results show the potential of baloncibart for people living with POTS and we look forward to advancing this novel therapy into a Phase 3 clinical trial in 2027.” The safety and efficacy of baloncibart have not been evaluated by any regulatory authority. About Regeneron’s VelocImmune Technology Regeneron’s VelocImmune technology utilizes a proprietary genetically engineered mouse platform endowed with a genetically humanized immune system to produce fully optimized human antibodies. When Regeneron’s Co-Founder, President and Chief Scientific Officer George D. Yancopoulos was a graduate student with his mentor, Frederick W. Alt in 1985, they were the first to envision making such a genetically humanized mouse, and Regeneron has spent decades inventing and developing VelocImmune and related VelociSuite ® technologies. Dr. Yancopoulos and his team have used VelocImmune technology to create a substantial proportion of all original, FDA-approved fully human monoclonal antibodies. This includes Dupixent ® (dupilumab), Libtayo ® (cemiplimab-rwlc), Praluent ® (alirocumab), Kevzara ® (sarilumab), Evkeeza ® (evinacumab-dgnb), Inmazeb ® (atoltivimab, maftivimab and odesivimab-ebgn), Veopoz ® (pozelimab-bbfg), and Pasatru ® (garetosmab-grts). In addition, REGEN-COV ® (casirivimab and imdevimab) had been authorized by the FDA during the COVID-19 pandemic until 2024. A total of 11 antibody and bispecific products have been approved or authorized worldwide that were invented or derived using VelocImmune technologies. About Regeneron Regeneron (NASDAQ: REGN) is a leading biotechnology company that invents, develops and commercializes life-transforming medicines for people with serious diseases. Founded and led by physician-scientists, our unique ability to repeatedly and consistently translate science into medicine has led to numerous approved treatments and product candidates in development, most of which were homegrown in our laboratories. Our medicines and pipeline are designed to help patients with eye diseases, allergic and inflammatory diseases, cancer, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurological diseases, hematologic conditions, infectious diseases, and rare diseases. Regeneron pushes the boundaries of scientific discovery and accelerates drug development using our proprietary technologies, such as VelociSuite ® , which produces optimized fully human antibodies and new classes of bispecific antibodies. We are shaping the next frontier of medicine with data-powered insights from the Regeneron Genetics Center ® and pioneering genetic medicine platforms, enabling us to identify innovative targets and complementary approaches to potentially treat or cure diseases. Data presented today for the first time at the American Autonomic Society (AAS) annual meeting POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) is a debilitating condition characterized by a marked increase in heart rate upon standing and associated orthostatic symptoms, with no FDA-approved treatments available A single dose of baloncibart reduced the exaggerated heart rate response to standing and improved orthostatic symptoms through four weeks; biomarker changes were consistent with plasma volume expansion, the intended effect of NPR1 blockade Potentially pivotal Phase 3 trial planned for first half of 2027 TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov.  12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. The data were presented for the first time at the American Autonomic Society’s (AAS) 37th International Symposium on the Autonomic Nervous System in San Diego, CA. POTS is a chronic disorder in which heart rate rises abnormally upon standing. Patients may experience palpitations, dizziness, fatigue, exercise intolerance, cognitive difficulties, gastrointestinal symptoms and chronic pain. Baloncibart is designed to increase the volume of blood in circulation in an effort to reduce the increase in heart rate and symptoms that occur in people with POTS. “POTS causes debilitating symptoms that can profoundly disrupt daily life, and patients have no FDA-approved treatment options. The LWPQ is a novel patient-reported outcome tool to assess POTS symptoms and function in clinical trials, which is being developed by Regeneron in accordance with the FDA patient-focused drug development guidance. Two serious TEAEs were reported: one case of headache with baloncibart 150 mg and one case of syncope with baloncibart 450 mg. Data presented today for the first time at the American Autonomic Society (AAS) annual meeting
POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) is a debilitating condition characterized by a marked increase in heart rate upon standing and associated orthostatic symptoms, with no FDA-approved treatments available
A single dose of baloncibart reduced the exaggerated heart rate response to standing and improved orthostatic symptoms through four weeks; biomarker changes were consistent with plasma volume expansion, the intended effect of NPR1 blockade
Potentially pivotal Phase 3 trial planned for first half of 2027
TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov.  12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced results from the Phase 2 PINNACLE trial in adults with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) evaluating baloncibart, a novel, investigational, first-in-class monoclonal antibody that blocks natriuretic peptide receptor 1 (NPR1). The data were presented for the first time at the American Autonomic Society’s (AAS) 37th International Symposium on the Autonomic Nervous System in San Diego, CA.
POTS is a chronic disorder in which heart rate rises abnormally upon standing. Patients may experience palpitations, dizziness, fatigue, exercise intolerance, cognitive difficulties, gastrointestinal symptoms and chronic pain. Although historically underdiagnosed, recent estimates suggest it affects between 500,000 and several million people in the U.S., and the vast majority are young women. While the cause of POTS is unknown, it is believed to be associated with low blood volume. Baloncibart is designed to increase the volume of blood in circulation in an effort to reduce the increase in heart rate and symptoms that occur in people with POTS.
“POTS causes debilitating symptoms that can profoundly disrupt daily life, and patients have no FDA-approved treatment options. In the trial, a single injection of baloncibart 450 mg reduced the exaggerated heart rate response to standing and improved orthostatic symptoms through four weeks,” said Satish R. Raj, M.D., Professor of Cardiac Science at the University of Calgary’s Cumming School of Medicine, and investigator in the trial. “The results are consistent with the rationale for NPR1 blockade in POTS, with biomarker changes pointing to an increase in blood volume alongside lower heart rate and better symptoms.”
The randomized, double-blind, Phase 2 PINNACLE trial evaluated a single subcutaneous dose of baloncibart 150 mg (n=27) or 450 mg (n=28) compared to placebo (n=27) in patients with POTS. The primary endpoint was the change in heart rate from lying down to standing (DeltaHR) at day 8; no formal hypothesis testing was prespecified. Improvements were observed with baloncibart on DeltaHR and other key measures of the disease (i.e., symptoms and function) as assessed by the Living With POTS Questionnaire (LWPQ). The LWPQ is a novel patient-reported outcome tool to assess POTS symptoms and function in clinical trials, which is being developed by Regeneron in accordance with the FDA patient-focused drug development guidance.
Baloncibart 450 mg reduced DeltaHR versus placebo at day 8 (primary endpoint) with a least-squares (LS) mean difference of -11.4 beats per minute (bpm; nominal p=0.0007), and at day 29 (secondary endpoint) with an LS mean difference of -7.4 bpm (nominal p=0.0124). Baloncibart 150 mg reduced DeltaHR versus placebo at day 8 (LS mean difference: -9.5 bpm; nominal p=0.0045), but the effect was not maintained at day 29.
Baloncibart 450 mg improved orthostatic symptoms, physical functioning, and activities of daily living versus placebo at day 29, as measured by the LWPQ. Domain scores range from 0 to 100, with lower scores indicating fewer symptoms or less impairment. The LS mean differences in change from baseline for each domain were as follows:
Orthostatic symptoms (baseline mean: 45.5): -12.9 points (nominal p=0.0096) Physical functioning (baseline mean: 55.1): -13.8 points (nominal p=0.0073) Activities of daily living (baseline mean: 48.7): -8.7 points (nominal p=0.1035) Overall across the three domains, there was no obvious improvement with baloncibart 150 mg compared to placebo
Orthostatic symptoms (baseline mean: 45.5): -12.9 points (nominal p=0.0096)
Physical functioning (baseline mean: 55.1): -13.8 points (nominal p=0.0073)
Activities of daily living (baseline mean: 48.7): -8.7 points (nominal p=0.1035)

Additionally at day 8, both doses of baloncibart led to changes in biomarkers consistent with the anticipated beneficial plasma volume expansion driven by NPR1 blockade, including an increase in NT-proBNP and reductions in standing norepinephrine and hemoglobin. Average standing systolic blood pressure increased for both doses, with observed mean changes from baseline at day 29 of 8.7 mmHg to a mean of 118.8 mmHg for baloncibart 450 mg and 5.4 mmHg to a mean of 114.0 mmHg for baloncibart 150 mg.
In the trial, single doses of baloncibart up to 450 mg were generally well tolerated. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were mostly mild or moderate and occurred in 13 patients (48.1%) receiving placebo, 18 patients (66.7%) receiving baloncibart 150 mg, and 19 (67.9%) receiving baloncibart 450 mg; one severe TEAE occurred in the trial in the placebo group. TEAEs that occurred in ≥10% of patients in any treatment group, including placebo, baloncibart 150 mg and baloncibart 450 mg, were: injection site reaction (14.8%, 3.7%, and 17.9%), headache (0%, 11.1%, and 10.7%), syncope (11.1%, 14.8%, and 3.6%), heavy menstrual bleeding (0%, 11.1%, and 0%), and nasopharyngitis (11.1%, 0%, and 0%). Two serious TEAEs were reported: one case of headache with baloncibart 150 mg and one case of syncope with baloncibart 450 mg. No TEAE led to discontinuation.
“POTS is a condition that disproportionately impacts younger women and has been under-recognized and under-served for too long, which is why it was critical to incorporate the patient experience in our trial design and measure symptoms that reflect how patients actually feel and function,” said Boaz Hirshberg, M.D., Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, Internal Medicine at Regeneron. “These initial results show the potential of baloncibart for people living with POTS and we look forward to advancing this novel therapy into a Phase 3 clinical trial in 2027.”
The safety and efficacy of baloncibart have not been evaluated by any regulatory authority.

Accessibility: Skip TopNav Commit Biologics nominates first development candidate from BiCE™, its complement system engaging platform, and strengthens senior leadership November 12, 2026 03:30 ET | Source: Commit Biologics Commit Biologics COM002 is a first-in-class complement-powered immune engager based on Commit Biologics’ proprietary BiCE™ platform. Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen appointed Chief Operating Officer and Dr. Benjamin Ole Wolthers as Head of Clinical Development, ahead of Phase 1 initiation. Both join Commit’s executive management team. Clinical trial preparations are underway, with first patient dosing expected in early 2028. COPENHAGEN, Denmark, Nov.  12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Commit Biologics (“Commit”), the biotechnology company pioneering complement-powered immune engagers, today announces the nomination of its first development candidate, as well as making two senior appointments, as it transitions from platform discovery to clinical development. COM002 is the first candidate to emerge from Commit’s proprietary Bispecific Complement Engager (BiCE™) platform, producing antibodies which harness the power of the complement system to safely target and eliminate specific cells. COM002 builds on Commit’s platform-validating data in non-human primates, announced in November 2025, which showed rapid, deep and sustained targeted B cell depletion with no treatment-related safety findings and without systemic cytokine release. During 2026, Commit has built the translational data package required to support COM002’s progression to the clinic, initially targeting relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with plans to expand into several autoimmune indications. Beyond COM002, Commit is advancing a growing pipeline of innovative therapies to unlock the broader potential of the BiCE™ platform across oncology and autoimmune diseases. Mikkel Wandahl Pedersen, CSO of Commit Biologics, said: “COM002 is our first clinical development candidate of an entirely new class of immune engagers, with potential applications in cancer and autoimmune disease. The nomination is a critical milestone, as we seek to show how our BiCE™ platform could revolutionise treatment, just as previous classes of immunotherapies, like T cell engagers and checkpoint inhibitors, have done.” Thomas L. F. Montgomery Andresen, CEO of Commit Biologics, said: “Nominating the first complement-powered immune engager is a pivotal moment for Commit, as we look ahead to taking COM002 into the clinic and unlock the potential of our BiCE™ platform. It is also a great pleasure to welcome two new members of our leadership team, who both have tremendous strengths and the hands-on experience that we need.” Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen, newly-appointed Chief Operating Officer, said: “Commit has an inspiring ambition to define a new category of medicine, and I look forward to ensuring we execute on our milestones to get BiCE™ antibodies to patients as fast as possible.” Benjamin Ole Wolthers, newly-appointed Head of Clinical Development, said: “ Being part of Commit’s pioneering effort using the complement system in immunotherapy is a privilege. Developing COM002 will be a great opportunity to showcase the treatment possibilities of this new drug class.” Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen brings 25 years of executive leadership in operations, commercial strategy and large-scale transformation. Most recently, she was Chief Operating Officer at Gubra. Before that, she was CEO of Innovation Fund Denmark, with a portfolio of around €1 billion, built Bavarian Nordic’s global commercial organisation, and spent 12 years in senior leadership roles at GSK. She holds an MSc in Physics from the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen. Benjamin Ole Wolthers is a physician scientist with strong international experience in drug development. His career started in frontline care of children with leukaemia at Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, and he later undertook development leadership at Kite Pharma, Galapagos and most recently Evaxion. At Kite and Galapagos, he led global teams responsible for early-stage and registrational CAR-T trials, while he oversaw clinical development strategy for first-in-human trials at Evaxion. At Commit, he will lead clinical development, translational medicine and regulatory strategy, and will lead COM002 into Phase 1 trials. For more information, please contact: Optimum Strategic Communications Nick Bastin, Stephen Adams, Aoife Minihan Tel: +44 (0) 204 566 8543 Email: commit@optimumcomms.com About Commit Biologics Commit Biologics is developing complement-powered immune engagers, a new class of immunotherapies for oncology, immunology & inflammation and beyond. Its proprietary Bispecific Complement Engager (BiCE™) platform turns IgG antibodies into potent, selective complement engagers that eliminate diseased cells independently of T cells. Founded by scientists from Aarhus University in Denmark, an internationally important centre for complement research for more than three decades, Commit is based in Copenhagen and Aarhus and backed by Novo Holdings, Bioqube Ventures, Korys and the BioInnovation Institute. www.commitbio.com About the complement system The complement system is a central part of the innate immune system, which has been conserved through more than a billion years of evolution. It is made up of more than 50 proteins which recognise threats, amplify immune responses and destroy pathogens and damaged cells. Complement is present in every person, acts within minutes and is continuously replenished, so it does not become exhausted the way T cells can. Until now, it has remained largely untapped as a way to target and remove diseased cells. While turning complement off through inhibition is an established mode of action for marketed products in complement-driven diseases, the ability to turn complement on – to remove diseased cells safely and selectively – has remained elusive. COPENHAGEN, Denmark, Nov.  12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Commit Biologics (“Commit”), the biotechnology company pioneering complement-powered immune engagers, today announces the nomination of its first development candidate, as well as making two senior appointments, as it transitions from platform discovery to clinical development.
COM002 is the first candidate to emerge from Commit’s proprietary Bispecific Complement Engager (BiCE™) platform, producing antibodies which harness the power of the complement system to safely target and eliminate specific cells. COM002 builds on Commit’s platform-validating data in non-human primates, announced in November 2025, which showed rapid, deep and sustained targeted B cell depletion with no treatment-related safety findings and without systemic cytokine release.
During 2026, Commit has built the translational data package required to support COM002’s progression to the clinic, initially targeting relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with plans to expand into several autoimmune indications.
Beyond COM002, Commit is advancing a growing pipeline of innovative therapies to unlock the broader potential of the BiCE™ platform across oncology and autoimmune diseases.
Mikkel Wandahl Pedersen, CSO of Commit Biologics, said: “COM002 is our first clinical development candidate of an entirely new class of immune engagers, with potential applications in cancer and autoimmune disease. The nomination is a critical milestone, as we seek to show how our BiCE™ platform could revolutionise treatment, just as previous classes of immunotherapies, like T cell engagers and checkpoint inhibitors, have done.”
Mikkel Wandahl Pedersen, CSO of Commit Biologics, said:
Thomas L. F. Montgomery Andresen, CEO of Commit Biologics, said: “Nominating the first complement-powered immune engager is a pivotal moment for Commit, as we look ahead to taking COM002 into the clinic and unlock the potential of our BiCE™ platform. It is also a great pleasure to welcome two new members of our leadership team, who both have tremendous strengths and the hands-on experience that we need.”
Thomas L. F. Montgomery Andresen, CEO of Commit Biologics, said:
Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen, newly-appointed Chief Operating Officer, said: “Commit has an inspiring ambition to define a new category of medicine, and I look forward to ensuring we execute on our milestones to get BiCE™ antibodies to patients as fast as possible.”
Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen, newly-appointed Chief Operating Officer, said:
Benjamin Ole Wolthers, newly-appointed Head of Clinical Development, said: “ Being part of Commit’s pioneering effort using the complement system in immunotherapy is a privilege. Developing COM002 will be a great opportunity to showcase the treatment possibilities of this new drug class.”
Benjamin Ole Wolthers, newly-appointed Head of Clinical Development, said: “
Anne-Marie Levy Rasmussen brings 25 years of executive leadership in operations, commercial strategy and large-scale transformation. Most recently, she was Chief Operating Officer at Gubra. Before that, she was CEO of Innovation Fund Denmark, with a portfolio of around €1 billion, built Bavarian Nordic’s global commercial organisation, and spent 12 years in senior leadership roles at GSK. She holds an MSc in Physics from the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen.
Benjamin Ole Wolthers is a physician scientist with strong international experience in drug development. His career started in frontline care of children with leukaemia at Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, and he later undertook development leadership at Kite Pharma, Galapagos and most recently Evaxion. At Kite and Galapagos, he led global teams responsible for early-stage and registrational CAR-T trials, while he oversaw clinical development strategy for first-in-human trials at Evaxion. At Commit, he will lead clinical development, translational medicine and regulatory strategy, and will lead COM002 into Phase 1 trials.

About Commit Biologics Commit Biologics is developing complement-powered immune engagers, a new class of immunotherapies for oncology, immunology & inflammation and beyond. Its proprietary Bispecific Complement Engager (BiCE™) platform turns IgG antibodies into potent, selective complement engagers that eliminate diseased cells independently of T cells. Founded by scientists from Aarhus University in Denmark, an internationally important centre for complement research for more than three decades, Commit is based in Copenhagen and Aarhus and backed by Novo Holdings, Bioqube Ventures, Korys and the BioInnovation Institute. www.commitbio.com
About Commit Biologics
About the complement system The complement system is a central part of the innate immune system, which has been conserved through more than a billion years of evolution. It is made up of more than 50 proteins which recognise threats, amplify immune responses and destroy pathogens and damaged cells. Complement is present in every person, acts within minutes and is continuously replenished, so it does not become exhausted the way T cells can. Until now, it has remained largely untapped as a way to target and remove diseased cells. While turning complement off through inhibition is an established mode of action for marketed products in complement-driven diseases, the ability to turn complement on – to remove diseased cells safely and selectively – has remained elusive.

Accessibility: Skip TopNav Cue Biopharma Announces Positive Topline Results from CUE-221 Phase 2 Study in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria Results support potential for differentiated clinical impact for patients suffering from chronic hives and advancement to Phase 2b/3 registration enabling study September 20, 2026 06:00 ET | Source: Cue Biopharma, Inc. Cue Biopharma, Inc. Primary endpoint and the key secondary endpoint were met with high statistical significance and CUE-221 demonstrated an overall favorable safety profile Clinically different efficacy profile observed relative to XOLAIR ® (omalizumab) highlights potential for a fundamental mechanism-based biological difference Cue Biopharma to host conference call on Monday, September 21, at 8:00 a.m. EDT BOSTON, Sept.  20, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cue Biopharma (Nasdaq: CUE), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company targeting transformative therapies for immune-mediated diseases, today announced positive topline results from the Phase 2 clinical trial of CUE-221 (UB-221) conducted in China by Genesis Life Sciences, a related company of Ascendant Health Limited (Ascendant). The trial enrolled 145 participants with moderate to severe chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), a disease resulting in chronic hives, that remained inadequately controlled despite treatment with H1 antihistamines. “We are excited to share these positive results which we believe establish CUE-221 as a potential best therapeutic option for patients suffering with chronic spontaneous urticaria,” said Shao-Lee Lin, M.D., Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Cue Biopharma. “These findings reinforce our enthusiasm for the precision engineered, unique dual mechanism of action of CUE-221, reflecting science that is truly differentiated. Based on the strength of these data, we are working toward the rapid initiation of a Phase 2b/3 study in CSU and continuing to advance a planned Phase 2 study in food allergy. We thank the patients, investigators, and study staff, all of whom made these results possible. We look forward to presenting the complete data set including PK and IgE analyses from this 36-week study at an upcoming scientific meeting.” Phase 2 CSU Study Topline Results The Phase 2 multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo and active comparator-controlled study was conducted in China and included a 16-week treatment period with a 20-week follow-up period post-treatment. Patients were randomized in a 2:2:2:1:1 ratio across five treatment groups to either subcutaneously deliver CUE-221 at 4 mg/kg, 2 mg/kg, or 1 mg/kg Q4W, or placebo Q4W, or omalizumab 300 mg Q4W. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients who achieved HSS7=0 at week 12. A key secondary endpoint assessed complete response, defined as the proportion of patients who achieved UAS7=0 at week 12. The study was designed to test superiority over placebo. Omalizumab was included to enable comparative efficacy without planned statistical testing. The primary endpoint of percentage of patients with HSS7=0 at week 12 was dose-responsive and met at all dose levels. The key secondary endpoint of percentage of patients with UAS7=0 at week 12 was dose responsive and met statistical significance at the 4 mg/kg highest dose level. Primary Endpoint of HSS7=0 at Week 12 CUE-221 (Q4W) Placebo Q4W Omalizumab Q4W 4 mg/kg (N=35) 2 mg/kg (N=36) 1 mg/kg (N=37) (N=18) 300 mg (N=17) Complete Resolution of Hives (HSS7=0) 54% 53% 43% 11% 41% 95% Confidence Interval (37%, 71%) (36%, 70%) (27%, 61%) (1%, 35%) (18%, 67%) P-values (vs placebo) p < 0.005 p < 0.005 p < 0.05 NA Not Tested P-values based on Fisher’s exact test; Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence interval Key Secondary Endpoint of UAS7=0 at Week 12 CUE-221 (Q4W) Placebo Q4W Omalizumab Q4W 4 mg/kg (N=35) 2 mg/kg (N=36) 1 mg/kg (N=37) N=18 300 mg (N=17) Complete Response (UAS7=0) 46% * 39% 38% 11% 29% 95% Confidence Interval (29%, 63%) (23%, 57%) (23%, 55%) (1%, 35%) (10%, 56%) * p<0.05 P-values based on Fisher’s exact test; Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence interval The percentage of participants who achieved HSS7=0 further increased beyond the Week 12 primary endpoint, peaking at Week 22 across all CUE-221 dose groups. After a last dose was administered for all groups at Week 16, clinically meaningful benefit was maintained for up to 12 weeks off treatment (through week 28) at the 4 mg/kg dose level. A higher rate of complete resolution of hives was observed for the 4 mg/kg dose group relative to the lower dose groups and placebo, and post hoc analysis at Week 28 demonstrated a statistically significant difference versus omalizumab (delta = 36%), supporting the premise of fundamental difference between CUE-221 and omalizumab with respect to impacts on disease biology. Complete Resolutions of Hives at Primary Endpoint, Peak Effect, and 12 Weeks Off Drug CUE-221 (Q4W) Placebo Q4W Omalizumab Q4W CUE 4mg/kg vs.Omalizumab Time 4 mg/kg 2mg/kg 1 mg/kg Placebo 300 mg Δ in Percent Week 12 Primary 54% 53% 43% 11% 41% 13% Week 22 Peak Effect 69% 61% 57% 11% 41% 28% Week 28 12 weeks off drug 60% 31% 24% 11% 24% 36% * * p<0.05 P-values based on Fisher’s exact test Demographics and baseline disease characteristics were generally well balanced across treatment groups. CUE-221 demonstrated a favorable safety profile. There were no treatment-related serious adverse events and no cases of hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis. Injection site reactions (ISR) were infrequent, only one ISR was > grade 1, and none led to study discontinuation. “The results of the Phase 2 CUE-221 study in patients with CSU are particularly notable,” said Dale Umetsu, M.D., Ph.D., Clinical Professor of Medicine and former Chief of the Allergy and Immunology Division, Stanford University, Clinical Professor of Pediatrics, University of California, San Francisco and prior Global Lead for XOLAIR development. “First, the results after 12 weeks of treatment, after three doses, appear to indicate that CUE-221 was better than XOLAIR for CSU at all dose levels tested. Moreover, there was persistent improvement with the 4 mg/kg dose at week 28, which was 12 weeks off treatment, significantly better than that off of standard XOLAIR dosing. Finally, the safety data analyzed so far, show no major safety issues, which is not unexpected from an anti-IgE mAb.” Dr. Umetsu added, “These results suggest that CUE-221, like XOLAIR is designed to prevent IgE from binding to FceR1 but unlike XOLAIR, allows IgE to bind to CD23, may represent a critical advancement over XOLAIR. The results support that the effects of CUE-221 on IgE function could result in substantial efficacy in CSU that persists for several months, even after dosing ends. Since XOLAIR has represented the clear standard for all other CSU therapies, the possibility that CUE-221 may represent a clear improvement above that of XOLAIR is most impressive. That improvement in efficacy may be directly relevant for food allergy, another area where XOLAIR currently prevails as the standard-of-care.“ “I am very pleased to see these outstanding results from the UB-221 Phase 2 CSU trial,” said Tse-Wen Chang, Ph.D., innovator of XOLAIR as well as UB-221 and an international expert in IgE biology. “The UB-221 data provide clear clinical evidence validating the molecule’s design to not only directly neutralize IgE, but also to create a next-generation approach to eliminate the production of new IgE over time. This fundamental difference in biological mechanism that is now clinically evident cannot be reached by giving higher doses or more potent IgE neutralization. Having invented several novel IgE-targeting molecules that ultimately led to the creation of UB-221, I am encouraged by these emerging data and the potential for this approach to offer a meaningfully different path toward a functional treatment for IgE-mediated diseases.” Webcast and Conference Call Cue Biopharma will host a conference call and webcast on Monday, September 21 at 8:00 a.m. EDT to present the results. The event will be webcast live and can be accessed via the attached link below. https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/mjexxy37 About Dale Umetsu, M.D., Ph.D. Dale Umetsu, M.D., Ph.D., Former chief of the allergy immunology division and tenured professor of pediatrics at Stanford University, and Former Prince al Saud Professor of Pediatrics AT Harvard Medical School. Dr. Umetsu also led global development of XOLAIR and the approval of XOLAIR for CSU and food allergy while at Genentech. Currently, he serves as a clinical professor of pediatrics at the University of California, San Francisco. About Tse-Wen Chang, Ph.D. Tse-Wen Chang, Ph.D., is a Taiwanese immunologist and pioneer in anti-IgE therapy. His early research into the immunoglobulin E (IgE) pathway and antibody-based therapeutics contributed to the development of omalizumab (XOLAIR), which is approved for the treatment of severe allergic asthma and severe chronic spontaneous urticaria. Dr. Chang is a cofounder of Tanox, a biopharmaceutical company focused on anti-IgE therapies for allergic diseases. He previously served as Dean of the College of Life Sciences at National Tsing Hua University in Taiwan and as Distinguished Research Fellow at the Genomics Research Center, Academia Sinica. About Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria CSU is a chronic inflammatory skin disease driven in part by type 2 inflammation, which causes sudden and debilitating hives and recurring itch. CSU is typically treated with H1 antihistamines, medicines that target H1 receptors on cells to control symptoms of itch and urticaria. However, the disease remains uncontrolled despite antihistamine treatment in many patients, some of whom are left with limited alternative treatment options. These individuals continue to experience symptoms that can be debilitating and significantly impact their quality of life. About CUE-221 CUE-221 (Ascendant-221, UB-221) is a humanized anti-IgE IgG1 monoclonal antibody designed with a precision engineered dual mechanism of action. CUE-221 binds to IgE at sites that are distinct from the binding sites for other anti-IgE monoclonal antibodies. In doing so, it maintains the capacity of total IgE to bind the CD23 receptor at the surface of B cells, resulting in reduced IgE synthesis. Therefore, CUE-221 is a functionally distinct novel anti-IgE antibody designed to not only neutralize free IgE with high potency, but also prevents the synthesis of new IgE which could ultimately result in functional cure if IgE is eradicated. The CUE-221 Phase 2 clinical trial in CSU produced positive topline results and clinical evidence providing initial validation of the clinical potential of a precision engineered anti-IgE dual mechanism of action. The study also demonstrated fundamental biological differences compared to current therapies. Based on these data, we are planning to advance CUE-221 in a Phase 2b/3 study in chronic spontaneous urticaria and in a Phase 2 study in food allergy. CUE-221 (UB-221) was innovated by Dr. Chang Tse Wen, a pioneer in the field of anti-IgE therapy, while serving as a Fellow of Academia Sinica. UB-221 was originally developed by United Biopharma (Holdings) Co., Ltd. (“United Biopharma”) with rights allocated between two of United Biopharma’s related companies, Genesis Life Sciences (“Genesis”) (China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, where Genesis continues development of the antibody under the name UB-221) and Ascendant Health Limited (“Ascendant”) (rest of world). Under an exclusive license agreement with Ascendant, Cue Biopharma obtained exclusive development, manufacturing, and commercialization rights in Ascendant’s rest of world territories. About Cue Biopharma Cue Biopharma (Nasdaq: CUE) is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on advancing a portfolio of potentially transformative therapies designed to enable functional cures across immunological disorders. Its lead asset, CUE-221, is a novel anti-IgE antibody with a dual mechanism of action design, moving into Phase 2b/3 development for allergic diseases. In addition, Cue developed the Immuno-STAT ® platform which selectively targets disease-specific T cells in vivo without broad immune modulation. Its lead autoimmune candidate, CUE-401, has an investigational new drug application pending in the U.S. for a Phase 1 clinical trial. CUE-401 is designed to regulate inflammation and drive Treg-mediated tolerance. Cue is led by an experienced management team with deep expertise in identifying, acquiring, and advancing promising drug candidates. About Ascendant Health Limited Ascendant is a privately held biotechnology company committed to delivering transformative solutions to patients globally. About Genesis Life Sciences Genesis Life Sciences focuses on the innovative development of monoclonal antibody drugs. It is a biopharmaceutical company with a product line in late-stage clinical trials, specializing in the development of innovative monoclonal antibody drugs applicable to chronic infectious diseases, allergic diseases, and autoimmune diseases. Closely aligned with key national research projects and market demand, the company has introduced highly promising monoclonal antibody products, leveraging internal research capabilities and support from expert teams across various fields to accelerate the product launch and sales process. We care about human health and well-being, focus on unmet patient needs, and drive monoclonal antibody development through innovative thinking, ultimately sharing our results with partners and the public, striving to provide the best treatment for patients. *XOLAIR ® is a registered trademark of Novartis AG. BOSTON, Sept.  20, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cue Biopharma (Nasdaq: CUE), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company targeting transformative therapies for immune-mediated diseases, today announced positive topline results from the Phase 2 clinical trial of CUE-221 (UB-221) conducted in China by Genesis Life Sciences, a related company of Ascendant Health Limited (Ascendant). The trial enrolled 145 participants with moderate to severe chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), a disease resulting in chronic hives, that remained inadequately controlled despite treatment with H1 antihistamines.
“We are excited to share these positive results which we believe establish CUE-221 as a potential best therapeutic option for patients suffering with chronic spontaneous urticaria,” said Shao-Lee Lin, M.D., Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Cue Biopharma. “These findings reinforce our enthusiasm for the precision engineered, unique dual mechanism of action of CUE-221, reflecting science that is truly differentiated. Based on the strength of these data, we are working toward the rapid initiation of a Phase 2b/3 study in CSU and continuing to advance a planned Phase 2 study in food allergy. We thank the patients, investigators, and study staff, all of whom made these results possible. We look forward to presenting the complete data set including PK and IgE analyses from this 36-week study at an upcoming scientific meeting.”
Phase 2 CSU Study Topline Results The Phase 2 multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo and active comparator-controlled study was conducted in China and included a 16-week treatment period with a 20-week follow-up period post-treatment. Patients were randomized in a 2:2:2:1:1 ratio across five treatment groups to either subcutaneously deliver CUE-221 at 4 mg/kg, 2 mg/kg, or 1 mg/kg Q4W, or placebo Q4W, or omalizumab 300 mg Q4W. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients who achieved HSS7=0 at week 12. A key secondary endpoint assessed complete response, defined as the proportion of patients who achieved UAS7=0 at week 12. The study was designed to test superiority over placebo. Omalizumab was included to enable comparative efficacy without planned statistical testing.

articles.title: Windward Bio Announces Closing of $251.2 Million Initial Public Offering and Concurrent Private Placement, Including Full Exercise of Underwriters’ Option to Purchase Additional Shares

Accessibility: Skip TopNav Windward Bio Announces Pricing of Initial Public Offering November 12, 2026 18:18 ET | Source: Windward Bio Group AG Windward Bio Group AG BASEL, Switzerland, Nov.  12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Windward Bio Group AG (“Windward”) (Nasdaq: WWB), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing ultra-long-acting antibody medicines for patients with serious respiratory and dermatologic diseases, today announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 10,294,117 common shares at a public offering price of $17.00 per share. In addition, Windward has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 1,544,117 common shares at the initial public offering price, less the underwriting discounts and commissions. The gross proceeds to Windward from the initial public offering and the concurrent private placement (see below), without giving effect to the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares and before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses, are expected to be $225.0 million. All of the common shares are being offered by Windward. In addition to the common shares sold in the initial public offering, Windward announced a concurrent sale of 1,532,691 common shares and pre-funded warrants to purchase 1,408,485 common shares, in each case at the initial public offering price per common share, in a private placement to Sanofi Foreign Participations B.V. for an aggregate purchase price of $50.0 million. The sale of the common shares and pre-funded warrants will not be registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). Windward’s shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 13, 2026 under the symbol “WWB.” The offering is expected to close on November 16, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Jefferies, TD Cowen, Piper Sandler and UBS Investment Bank are acting as joint book-running managers for the offering. A registration statement relating to the shares being sold in the initial public offering has been filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and was declared effective on November 12, 2026. The offering of the shares is being made only by means of a prospectus forming part of the effective registration statement relating to these shares. Copies of the final prospectus, when available, may be obtained from Jefferies LLC, Attention: Equity Syndicate Prospectus Department, 520 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10022, by telephone at 877-821-7388, or by email at prospectus_department@jefferies.com; TD Securities (USA) LLC, Attn: c/o Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, NY 11717, or by email at TDManualrequest@broadridge.com; Piper Sandler & Co., Attention: Prospectus Department, 350 North 5th Street, Suite 1000, Minneapolis, MN 55401, by telephone at (800) 747-3924, or by email at prospectus@psc.com or UBS Securities LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 11 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10010, by email at ol-prospectus-request@ubs.com. The concurrent private placement is also scheduled to close on November 16, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The closing of the private placement is contingent and conditioned on consummation of the initial public offering. However, the closing of the initial public offering is not contingent on the consummation of the concurrent private placement. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell, or a solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any offer or sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to the registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. Accessibility: Skip TopNav PRISM MarketView Highlights Five Innovative Public Companies Supporting Strength and Mobility for National Physical Therapy Month October 22, 2026 12:17 ET | Source: PRISM MarketView PRISM MarketView New York OrthoPediatrics, Omada Health, Enovis, Myomo and FIGS span the full arc of physical therapy, from childhood care and prevention to recovery and the professionals who deliver it NEW YORK, Oct.  22, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- PRISM MarketView , a financial media platform covering small and micro-cap public companies, today published a feature marking National Physical Therapy Month. This year’s theme from the American Physical Therapy Association , “PT For Future Me,” focuses on building strength, mobility and resilience across a lifetime to extend health span, the years people spend healthy and free of preventable chronic disease. PRISM’s feature highlights five public companies working on different stages of that journey. Starting Young: OrthoPediatrics (NASDAQ: KIDS) OrthoPediatrics focuses entirely on pediatric orthopedics, from trauma and deformity correction to scoliosis and specialty bracing. Many of the procedures it supports are followed by physical therapy, and the outcomes shape a child’s mobility for decades. Staying Strong: Omada Health (NASDAQ: OMDA) Omada Health ’s GLP-1 Care Track includes a personalized exercise plan developed by a physical therapist to help protect muscle during weight loss. In a 12-week study published in Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism, members lost 6.0% of their starting weight, versus 3.3% with usual care, while gaining more muscle mass. Omada also runs a virtual musculoskeletal program with licensed physical therapists. Before and After Surgery: Enovis (NYSE: ENOV) Enovis ’s Prevention & Recovery business provides orthopedic and recovery solutions spanning injury prevention through rehabilitation, and its joint replacement implants are almost always followed by physical therapy. Second-quarter net sales were $583 million, up 5% on an organic basis. Restoring Function: Myomo (NYSE American: MYO) Myomo makes the MyoPro, a powered upper-limb orthosis that helps restore function to weakened or paralyzed arms after stroke, spinal cord injury and other neuromuscular conditions. Second-quarter revenue rose 21% to $11.71 million, with record orders of 255 units. Outfitting the Profession: FIGS (NYSE: FIGS) APTA’s campaign also celebrates the professionals who make physical therapy work. FIGS , a healthcare apparel brand built around healthcare professionals, grew second-quarter net revenues 28.8% to $196.6 million and reached 3.1 million active customers.
