Zymeworks Inc. 2026 financial guidance raised to a total revenue range of $337 million to $351 million (previously between $278 million and $292 million) and an Adjusted EBITDA range of $176 million to $190 mi llion (previously between $114 mill ion and $128 million) Ziihera ® first-line advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA) approval by the U.S. FDA expands royalty opportunity and provided a $250 million U.S. approval milestone Collaboration agreement with Roche, once Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976 clearance obtained, will provide a pathway for ZW209 value creation from capital-efficient R&D while preserving meaningful long-term economic participation The Company plans to host an R&D Day in New York on February 11 th , 2027 VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov.  09, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zymeworks Inc. (Nasdaq: ZYME), a biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets, while developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided a summary of recent business highlights. The Company has elected not to host a third quarter earnings conference call after release of its financial results. "We are entering the next phase of Zymeworks growth with a fundamentally stronger and more diversified business. The transformation of Zymeworks is becoming increasingly visible in our financial profile and in the breadth of opportunities available to us," said Kenneth Galbraith, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Zymeworks. "Over the course of 2026, Ziihera has expanded its label into first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, we have completed the acquisition of Theravance Biopharma, adding a recurring commercial cash-flow stream through YUPELRI. We have also made progress on strategic transactions that can expand the opportunities for our R&D portfolio, while reducing risk, maintaining R&D discipline, and adding potential future milestones and royalties. We are pleased to report an increase in our financial guidance for 2026 as a result of this business development execution. These advancements demonstrate the strategy we set out a year ago – to build a durable financial foundation through partnered and commercial assets, while maintaining the ability to create additional value through R&D, acquisitions, partnerships and disciplined capital allocation." Financial Highlights Royalty revenue from Jazz Pharmaceuticals (Jazz) and BeOne Medicines (BeOne) was $2.3 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven primarily by net product sales of Ziihera by Jazz in the United States. YUPELRI ® collaboration revenue increased 4% year-over-year (YoY). Quarterly U.S. net sales of $71.5 million for YUPELRI, recognized by Viatris, in 3Q-2026, increasing 0.2% YoY (3Q-2026 vs 3Q-2025). Increased doses of YUPELRI pulled through the hospital channel grew at a double-digit rate YoY, reflecting continued underlying momentum. Theravance Biopharma contributed approximately $1.5 million of revenue during the quarter, reflecting seven days of ownership following the September 23, 2026 acquisition date. Under the terms of our collaboration with Jazz, Zymeworks received a $250 million milestone payment related to Ziihera' s U.S. FDA approval for first-line treatment of HER2-positive advanced GEA in October 2026. Zymeworks remains eligible for up to $190 million in potential additional global regulatory milestones related to ex-U.S. approvals for Ziihera in HER2-positive GEA from Jazz and BeOne. During 2026, Zymeworks has accessed $600 million of non-dilutive financing through a non-recourse royalty-backed note, and a non-recourse note, with a weighted average cost of capital of less than 10%. The financing supported the Theravance Biopharma acquisition and the Company's share repurchase program while minimizing equity dilution. The Company currently has no current plans for additional equity issuances. Repurchased 534,381 shares for $14.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, with total share repurchases of 5,737,790 shares for $140.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 at an average price of $24.48 per share (exclusive of commission expense and estimated excise tax). The Company has increased its 2026 financial guidance for total revenue to be between $337 million and $351 million (previously between $278 million and $292 million) and adjusted EBITDA to be between $176 million and $190 million (previously between $114 million and $128 million), excluding the impact of any future transactions. This financial guidance is subject to expiration or termination of the waiting period under HSR as it relates to the Roche collaboration, expected during the fourth quarter of 2026. Business Highlights Expanding Revenue Diversification Through Theravance Biopharma Acquisition On September 23, 2026, Zymeworks completed the previously announced acquisition of Theravance Biopharma. With the completion of the transaction, Theravance Biopharma is now part of Zymeworks, further advancing Zymeworks’ strategy to build a diversified revenue-generating biotechnology company, combining innovative R&D with growing commercial and royalty-based cash flows. Post-closing, we expect $13 million to $15 million of annualized overhead and corporate costs to be eliminated, reducing future operating expenses. On September 28, 2026 , Zymeworks announced the appointment of Stuart Knight as Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer, as well as Jesse Fecker as Vice President of Intellectual Property, both of whom join Zymeworks from Theravance Biopharma. On October 19, 2026 , Zymeworks announced the appointment of Suzanne Monahan as Senior Vice President and General Manager, Theravance Biopharma. Recent Developments Recent key developments related to our portfolio are discussed below: Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) On August 25, 2026, our partner Jazz received U.S. FDA approval for two Ziihera -containing regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive GEA. Jazz subsequently launched U.S. commercialization, and secured a recommendation in the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines, as well as a Category 2A recommendation from the National Comprehensive Cancer Network ® (NCCN), positioning Ziihera as a preferred treatment for first-line GEA patients. On October 23, 2026, results from the second interim, and final formal, analysis of HERIZON-GEA-01 were presented as a late-breaking rapid oral presentation at the ESMO Annual Congress 2026. Key findings include: Nearly 40% of patients alive at three years with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, achieving a median overall survival (OS) of 27 months. Mature HERIZON-GEA-01 results show Ziihera plus chemotherapy delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS benefit, reducing the rate of death by 24% versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy regimen reduced the risk of death by 35% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52–0.80), improving from an HR of 0.72 at the first interim analysis. Other Partnered Programs ZW209 On October 23, 2026, Zymeworks announced an exclusive global collaboration and license agreement with Roche for the development of ZW209 . Under the agreement, Zymeworks is eligible to receive an upfront payment of $55 million, a $40 million payment upon initiation of the Phase 1b trial, additional development, commercial and sales-based milestone payments of up to $718 million, and tiered high single digit to mid-teens royalties on future net sales of any approved medicines resulting from the collaboration. This transaction is subject to the expiration or termination of the waiting period under HSR. ZW209 has received Investigational New Drug clearance from the U.S. FDA. We anticipate initiating a Phase 1, open-label, multicenter, global study in 2026 investigating ZW209 in collaboration with Roche to evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary anti-tumor activity. Roche will fund the Phase 1a trial and be responsible for subsequent global development and commercialization of ZW209. “Importantly, this collaboration with Roche demonstrates how the components of our business model work together in practice. By combining recurring commercial cash flows with a disciplined approach to R&D and partnerships, we are building a business model that can generate value through multiple pathways,” said Kenneth Galbraith. “Recurring cash flows provide greater flexibility to invest selectively in programs and opportunities with meaningful value-creation potential, while our R&D engine and business development activities create additional opportunities to generate milestones, royalties, licensing proceeds and other sources of long-term value. Just as importantly, we can increasingly match the capital and ownership structure to each opportunity, whether acquiring and operating a business, partnering an asset, licensing a program or bringing in external venture capital, without assuming that every opportunity must be funded entirely from our balance sheet.” Pasritamig On November 7, 2026, our partner Johnson & Johnson presented new data on the Phase 1 study of pasritamig (KLK2×CD3) in combination with JNJ-9401 (PSMA×CD28) at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC). Results demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: At the recommended Phase 2 regimen, the combination achieved a 73% PSA50 response rate, 47% PSA90 response rate, and undetectable PSA in 27% of patients, with responses ongoing beyond six months in all four patients achieving undetectable PSA. The combination maintained a favorable safety profile, with no Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events, no Grade ≥2 CRS and no treatment discontinuations at the recommended regimen. Wholly-Owned R&D Pipeline On October 24, 2026, Zymeworks presented new Phase 1 data for folate receptor alpha-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, ZW191 , at the ESMO Annual Congress. Updated data presented for ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha expression levels: Confirmed objective response rates of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups. Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration. On November 7, 2026, Zymeworks presented preclinical data at SITC on a novel PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 multispecific antibody with optimized geometry that achieves targeting of IL-7 to PD-1+ T cells. The poster presentation titled “Engineering targeted IL-7 delivery to enhance anti-tumor T cell fitness and persistence” shows that combining checkpoint and angiogenesis blockade with a T cell cytokine signal, PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 represents a mechanistically distinct strategy to improve the durability of anti-tumor responses. On December 13, 2026, Zymeworks will present new preclinical data for a penta-specific antibody at the American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting and Exhibition via a poster presentation titled “ZW1953: A multispecific T cell engager targeting FLT3, CLEC12A, and CD33 with conditional CD28 co-stimulation designed to overcome resistance mechanisms and improve treatment responses in AML”, representing the first scientific disclosure for Zymeworks in a hematological cancer indication. The Company plans to host a R&D Day on February 11 th , 2027 in New York, NY. A live webcast of the event will be accessible through Zymeworks' Investor Relations website at ir.zymeworks.com . A detailed agenda, including registration and dial-in information, will be provided closer to the event. Financial Results for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026 The key financial highlights for our 2026 third quarter results are as follows: Theravance Biopharma Acquisition – The acquisition of Theravance Biopharma closed on September 23, 2026 and had a limited impact on third quarter operating results given the timing of the transaction. Theravance Biopharma contributed approximately $1.5 million of revenue during the quarter, reflecting seven days of ownership following the acquisition date. The primary earnings impact related to integration and transaction-related costs associated with the acquisition. Revenue – Total revenue was $256.5 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $27.6 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to the $250.0 million milestone earned from Jazz following the U.S. approval of Ziihera for first-line HER2-positive GEA in August 2026. The increase was partially offset by the absence of a $25.0 million development milestone from Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine recognized during the third quarter of 2025. Research and Development (R&D) Expenses – R&D expenses were $36.1 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $35.6 million for the same period in 2025. R&D expenses were generally consistent with the prior year period, as lower spending on ZW171 following discontinuation of the program in 2025 and reduced spending on certain preclinical programs after completion of IND-enabling activities were largely offset by employee-related costs associated with the Theravance Biopharma acquisition. Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses – SG&A expenses were $42.7 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $14.1 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by costs associated with the Theravance Biopharma acquisition, including severance and transaction-related professional fees, together with higher stock-based compensation expense associated with 2026 equity awards, including leadership transition awards and the settlement of certain Theravance Biopharma equity awards. Other Income, net – Net other expense was $4.4 million in 3Q-2026, compared to net other income of $3.8 million for the same period in 2025. The change was driven primarily by interest expense related to the royalty-backed note financing arrangement with Royalty Pharma executed in March 2026 and lower interest income resulting from reduced investment balances. Net Loss – Net income was $173.7 million in 3Q-2026, compared to a net loss of $19.6 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was driven primarily by the $250.0 million milestone earned from Jazz following U.S. approval of Ziihera for first-line HER2-positive GEA in August 2026, partially offset by nonrecurring acquisition related costs and interest expense associated with the Company's royalty-based note financing arrangement with Royalty Pharma in March 2026. Since initiating its share repurchase program in August 2024, the Company has cumulatively utilized $279.8 million to reacquire 12,940,827 shares at an average price of $21.63 per share (exclusive of commission expense and estimated excise tax). As of November 6, 2026, the Company had approximately 69.0 million common shares outstanding. About Zymeworks Inc. Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI ® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera ® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies. Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. These capabilities, together with Zymeworks’ integrated drug development expertise, enable the Company to develop differentiated therapeutics and create value through both internal innovation and strategic partnerships. For more information about Zymeworks, its portfolio and pipeline, visit www.zymeworks.com and follow @ZymeworksInc on X. Business Highlights Expanding Revenue Diversification Through Theravance Biopharma Acquisition On September 23, 2026, Zymeworks completed the previously announced acquisition of Theravance Biopharma. With the completion of the transaction, Theravance Biopharma is now part of Zymeworks, further advancing Zymeworks’ strategy to build a diversified revenue-generating biotechnology company, combining innovative R&D with growing commercial and royalty-based cash flows. Post-closing, we expect $13 million to $15 million of annualized overhead and corporate costs to be eliminated, reducing future operating expenses. On September 28, 2026 , Zymeworks announced the appointment of Stuart Knight as Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer, as well as Jesse Fecker as Vice President of Intellectual Property, both of whom join Zymeworks from Theravance Biopharma. On October 19, 2026 , Zymeworks announced the appointment of Suzanne Monahan as Senior Vice President and General Manager, Theravance Biopharma. Recent Developments Recent key developments related to our portfolio are discussed below: Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) On August 25, 2026, our partner Jazz received U.S. FDA approval for two Ziihera -containing regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive GEA. Jazz subsequently launched U.S. commercialization, and secured a recommendation in the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines, as well as a Category 2A recommendation from the National Comprehensive Cancer Network ® (NCCN), positioning Ziihera as a preferred treatment for first-line GEA patients. On October 23, 2026, results from the second interim, and final formal, analysis of HERIZON-GEA-01 were presented as a late-breaking rapid oral presentation at the ESMO Annual Congress 2026. Key findings include: Nearly 40% of patients alive at three years with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, achieving a median overall survival (OS) of 27 months. Mature HERIZON-GEA-01 results show Ziihera plus chemotherapy delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS benefit, reducing the rate of death by 24% versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy regimen reduced the risk of death by 35% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52–0.80), improving from an HR of 0.72 at the first interim analysis. Other Partnered Programs ZW209 On October 23, 2026, Zymeworks announced an exclusive global collaboration and license agreement with Roche for the development of ZW209 . Under the agreement, Zymeworks is eligible to receive an upfront payment of $55 million, a $40 million payment upon initiation of the Phase 1b trial, additional development, commercial and sales-based milestone payments of up to $718 million, and tiered high single digit to mid-teens royalties on future net sales of any approved medicines resulting from the collaboration. This transaction is subject to the expiration or termination of the waiting period under HSR. ZW209 has received Investigational New Drug clearance from the U.S. FDA. We anticipate initiating a Phase 1, open-label, multicenter, global study in 2026 investigating ZW209 in collaboration with Roche to evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary anti-tumor activity. Roche will fund the Phase 1a trial and be responsible for subsequent global development and commercialization of ZW209. “Importantly, this collaboration with Roche demonstrates how the components of our business model work together in practice. By combining recurring commercial cash flows with a disciplined approach to R&D and partnerships, we are building a business model that can generate value through multiple pathways,” said Kenneth Galbraith. “Recurring cash flows provide greater flexibility to invest selectively in programs and opportunities with meaningful value-creation potential, while our R&D engine and business development activities create additional opportunities to generate milestones, royalties, licensing proceeds and other sources of long-term value. Just as importantly, we can increasingly match the capital and ownership structure to each opportunity, whether acquiring and operating a business, partnering an asset, licensing a program or bringing in external venture capital, without assuming that every opportunity must be funded entirely from our balance sheet.” Pasritamig On November 7, 2026, our partner Johnson & Johnson presented new data on the Phase 1 study of pasritamig (KLK2×CD3) in combination with JNJ-9401 (PSMA×CD28) at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC). Results demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: At the recommended Phase 2 regimen, the combination achieved a 73% PSA50 response rate, 47% PSA90 response rate, and undetectable PSA in 27% of patients, with responses ongoing beyond six months in all four patients achieving undetectable PSA. The combination maintained a favorable safety profile, with no Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events, no Grade ≥2 CRS and no treatment discontinuations at the recommended regimen. Wholly-Owned R&D Pipeline On October 24, 2026, Zymeworks presented new Phase 1 data for folate receptor alpha-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, ZW191 , at the ESMO Annual Congress. Updated data presented for ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha expression levels: Confirmed objective response rates of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups. Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration. On November 7, 2026, Zymeworks presented preclinical data at SITC on a novel PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 multispecific antibody with optimized geometry that achieves targeting of IL-7 to PD-1+ T cells. The poster presentation titled “Engineering targeted IL-7 delivery to enhance anti-tumor T cell fitness and persistence” shows that combining checkpoint and angiogenesis blockade with a T cell cytokine signal, PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 represents a mechanistically distinct strategy to improve the durability of anti-tumor responses. On December 13, 2026, Zymeworks will present new preclinical data for a penta-specific antibody at the American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting and Exhibition via a poster presentation titled “ZW1953: A multispecific T cell engager targeting FLT3, CLEC12A, and CD33 with conditional CD28 co-stimulation designed to overcome resistance mechanisms and improve treatment responses in AML”, representing the first scientific disclosure for Zymeworks in a hematological cancer indication. On September 28, 2026 , Zymeworks announced the appointment of Stuart Knight as Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer, as well as Jesse Fecker as Vice President of Intellectual Property, both of whom join Zymeworks from Theravance Biopharma. On October 19, 2026 , Zymeworks announced the appointment of Suzanne Monahan as Senior Vice President and General Manager, Theravance Biopharma. Recent Developments Recent key developments related to our portfolio are discussed below: Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) On August 25, 2026, our partner Jazz received U.S. FDA approval for two Ziihera -containing regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive GEA. Jazz subsequently launched U.S. commercialization, and secured a recommendation in the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines, as well as a Category 2A recommendation from the National Comprehensive Cancer Network ® (NCCN), positioning Ziihera as a preferred treatment for first-line GEA patients. On October 23, 2026, results from the second interim, and final formal, analysis of HERIZON-GEA-01 were presented as a late-breaking rapid oral presentation at the ESMO Annual Congress 2026. Key findings include: Nearly 40% of patients alive at three years with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, achieving a median overall survival (OS) of 27 months. Mature HERIZON-GEA-01 results show Ziihera plus chemotherapy delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS benefit, reducing the rate of death by 24% versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy regimen reduced the risk of death by 35% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52–0.80), improving from an HR of 0.72 at the first interim analysis. Other Partnered Programs ZW209 On October 23, 2026, Zymeworks announced an exclusive global collaboration and license agreement with Roche for the development of ZW209 . Under the agreement, Zymeworks is eligible to receive an upfront payment of $55 million, a $40 million payment upon initiation of the Phase 1b trial, additional development, commercial and sales-based milestone payments of up to $718 million, and tiered high single digit to mid-teens royalties on future net sales of any approved medicines resulting from the collaboration. This transaction is subject to the expiration or termination of the waiting period under HSR. ZW209 has received Investigational New Drug clearance from the U.S. FDA. We anticipate initiating a Phase 1, open-label, multicenter, global study in 2026 investigating ZW209 in collaboration with Roche to evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary anti-tumor activity. Roche will fund the Phase 1a trial and be responsible for subsequent global development and commercialization of ZW209. “Importantly, this collaboration with Roche demonstrates how the components of our business model work together in practice. By combining recurring commercial cash flows with a disciplined approach to R&D and partnerships, we are building a business model that can generate value through multiple pathways,” said Kenneth Galbraith. “Recurring cash flows provide greater flexibility to invest selectively in programs and opportunities with meaningful value-creation potential, while our R&D engine and business development activities create additional opportunities to generate milestones, royalties, licensing proceeds and other sources of long-term value. Just as importantly, we can increasingly match the capital and ownership structure to each opportunity, whether acquiring and operating a business, partnering an asset, licensing a program or bringing in external venture capital, without assuming that every opportunity must be funded entirely from our balance sheet.” Pasritamig On November 7, 2026, our partner Johnson & Johnson presented new data on the Phase 1 study of pasritamig (KLK2×CD3) in combination with JNJ-9401 (PSMA×CD28) at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC). Results demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: At the recommended Phase 2 regimen, the combination achieved a 73% PSA50 response rate, 47% PSA90 response rate, and undetectable PSA in 27% of patients, with responses ongoing beyond six months in all four patients achieving undetectable PSA. The combination maintained a favorable safety profile, with no Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events, no Grade ≥2 CRS and no treatment discontinuations at the recommended regimen. Wholly-Owned R&D Pipeline On October 24, 2026, Zymeworks presented new Phase 1 data for folate receptor alpha-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, ZW191 , at the ESMO Annual Congress. Updated data presented for ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha expression levels: Confirmed objective response rates of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups. Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration. On November 7, 2026, Zymeworks presented preclinical data at SITC on a novel PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 multispecific antibody with optimized geometry that achieves targeting of IL-7 to PD-1+ T cells. The poster presentation titled “Engineering targeted IL-7 delivery to enhance anti-tumor T cell fitness and persistence” shows that combining checkpoint and angiogenesis blockade with a T cell cytokine signal, PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 represents a mechanistically distinct strategy to improve the durability of anti-tumor responses. On December 13, 2026, Zymeworks will present new preclinical data for a penta-specific antibody at the American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting and Exhibition via a poster presentation titled “ZW1953: A multispecific T cell engager targeting FLT3, CLEC12A, and CD33 with conditional CD28 co-stimulation designed to overcome resistance mechanisms and improve treatment responses in AML”, representing the first scientific disclosure for Zymeworks in a hematological cancer indication. Results demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: At the recommended Phase 2 regimen, the combination achieved a 73% PSA50 response rate, 47% PSA90 response rate, and undetectable PSA in 27% of patients, with responses ongoing beyond six months in all four patients achieving undetectable PSA. Wholly-Owned R&D Pipeline On October 24, 2026, Zymeworks presented new Phase 1 data for folate receptor alpha-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, ZW191 , at the ESMO Annual Congress. Updated data presented for ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha expression levels: Confirmed objective response rates of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups. Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration. R&D expenses were generally consistent with the prior year period, as lower spending on ZW171 following discontinuation of the program in 2025 and reduced spending on certain preclinical programs after completion of IND-enabling activities were largely offset by employee-related costs associated with the Theravance Biopharma acquisition. Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses – SG&A expenses were $42.7 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $14.1 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by costs associated with the Theravance Biopharma acquisition, including severance and transaction-related professional fees, together with higher stock-based compensation expense associated with 2026 equity awards, including leadership transition awards and the settlement of certain Theravance Biopharma equity awards. Other Income, net – Net other expense was $4.4 million in 3Q-2026, compared to net other income of $3.8 million for the same period in 2025. The change was driven primarily by interest expense related to the royalty-backed note financing arrangement with Royalty Pharma executed in March 2026 and lower interest income resulting from reduced investment balances. Net Loss – Net income was $173.7 million in 3Q-2026, compared to a net loss of $19.6 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was driven primarily by the $250.0 million milestone earned from Jazz following U.S. approval of Ziihera for first-line HER2-positive GEA in August 2026, partially offset by nonrecurring acquisition related costs and interest expense associated with the Company's royalty-based note financing arrangement with Royalty Pharma in March 2026. Since initiating its share repurchase program in August 2024, the Company has cumulatively utilized $279.8 million to reacquire 12,940,827 shares at an average price of $21.63 per share (exclusive of commission expense and estimated excise tax). As of November 6, 2026, the Company had approximately 69.0 million common shares outstanding. About Zymeworks Inc. Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI ® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera ® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies. Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov.  09, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zymeworks Inc. (Nasdaq: ZYME), a biotechnology company managing a portfolio of licensed healthcare assets, while developing a diverse pipeline of novel, multifunctional biotherapeutics, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided a summary of recent business highlights. The Company has elected not to host a third quarter earnings conference call after release of its financial results.
"We are entering the next phase of Zymeworks growth with a fundamentally stronger and more diversified business. The transformation of Zymeworks is becoming increasingly visible in our financial profile and in the breadth of opportunities available to us," said Kenneth Galbraith, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Zymeworks. "Over the course of 2026, Ziihera has expanded its label into first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, we have completed the acquisition of Theravance Biopharma, adding a recurring commercial cash-flow stream through YUPELRI. We have also made progress on strategic transactions that can expand the opportunities for our R&D portfolio, while reducing risk, maintaining R&D discipline, and adding potential future milestones and royalties. We are pleased to report an increase in our financial guidance for 2026 as a result of this business development execution. These advancements demonstrate the strategy we set out a year ago – to build a durable financial foundation through partnered and commercial assets, while maintaining the ability to create additional value through R&D, acquisitions, partnerships and disciplined capital allocation."
Financial Highlights
Royalty revenue from Jazz Pharmaceuticals (Jazz) and BeOne Medicines (BeOne) was $2.3 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, driven primarily by net product sales of Ziihera by Jazz in the United States. YUPELRI ® collaboration revenue increased 4% year-over-year (YoY). Quarterly U.S. net sales of $71.5 million for YUPELRI, recognized by Viatris, in 3Q-2026, increasing 0.2% YoY (3Q-2026 vs 3Q-2025). Increased doses of YUPELRI pulled through the hospital channel grew at a double-digit rate YoY, reflecting continued underlying momentum. Theravance Biopharma contributed approximately $1.5 million of revenue during the quarter, reflecting seven days of ownership following the September 23, 2026 acquisition date. Under the terms of our collaboration with Jazz, Zymeworks received a $250 million milestone payment related to Ziihera' s U.S. FDA approval for first-line treatment of HER2-positive advanced GEA in October 2026. Zymeworks remains eligible for up to $190 million in potential additional global regulatory milestones related to ex-U.S. approvals for Ziihera in HER2-positive GEA from Jazz and BeOne. During 2026, Zymeworks has accessed $600 million of non-dilutive financing through a non-recourse royalty-backed note, and a non-recourse note, with a weighted average cost of capital of less than 10%. The financing supported the Theravance Biopharma acquisition and the Company's share repurchase program while minimizing equity dilution. The Company currently has no current plans for additional equity issuances. Repurchased 534,381 shares for $14.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, with total share repurchases of 5,737,790 shares for $140.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 at an average price of $24.48 per share (exclusive of commission expense and estimated excise tax). The Company has increased its 2026 financial guidance for total revenue to be between $337 million and $351 million (previously between $278 million and $292 million) and adjusted EBITDA to be between $176 million and $190 million (previously between $114 million and $128 million), excluding the impact of any future transactions. This financial guidance is subject to expiration or termination of the waiting period under HSR as it relates to the Roche collaboration, expected during the fourth quarter of 2026.

Recent Developments
Recent key developments related to our portfolio are discussed below:
Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii)
On August 25, 2026, our partner Jazz received U.S. FDA approval for two Ziihera -containing regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive GEA. Jazz subsequently launched U.S. commercialization, and secured a recommendation in the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines, as well as a Category 2A recommendation from the National Comprehensive Cancer Network ® (NCCN), positioning Ziihera as a preferred treatment for first-line GEA patients. On October 23, 2026, results from the second interim, and final formal, analysis of HERIZON-GEA-01 were presented as a late-breaking rapid oral presentation at the ESMO Annual Congress 2026. Key findings include: Nearly 40% of patients alive at three years with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, achieving a median overall survival (OS) of 27 months. Mature HERIZON-GEA-01 results show Ziihera plus chemotherapy delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS benefit, reducing the rate of death by 24% versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy regimen reduced the risk of death by 35% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52–0.80), improving from an HR of 0.72 at the first interim analysis.

Other Partnered Programs
ZW209
On October 23, 2026, Zymeworks announced an exclusive global collaboration and license agreement with Roche for the development of ZW209 . Under the agreement, Zymeworks is eligible to receive an upfront payment of $55 million, a $40 million payment upon initiation of the Phase 1b trial, additional development, commercial and sales-based milestone payments of up to $718 million, and tiered high single digit to mid-teens royalties on future net sales of any approved medicines resulting from the collaboration. This transaction is subject to the expiration or termination of the waiting period under HSR. ZW209 has received Investigational New Drug clearance from the U.S. FDA. We anticipate initiating a Phase 1, open-label, multicenter, global study in 2026 investigating ZW209 in collaboration with Roche to evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary anti-tumor activity. Roche will fund the Phase 1a trial and be responsible for subsequent global development and commercialization of ZW209.

Just as importantly, we can increasingly match the capital and ownership structure to each opportunity, whether acquiring and operating a business, partnering an asset, licensing a program or bringing in external venture capital, without assuming that every opportunity must be funded entirely from our balance sheet.”
Pasritamig
On November 7, 2026, our partner Johnson & Johnson presented new data on the Phase 1 study of pasritamig (KLK2×CD3) in combination with JNJ-9401 (PSMA×CD28) at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC). Results demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer:
At the recommended Phase 2 regimen, the combination achieved a 73% PSA50 response rate, 47% PSA90 response rate, and undetectable PSA in 27% of patients, with responses ongoing beyond six months in all four patients achieving undetectable PSA. The combination maintained a favorable safety profile, with no Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events, no Grade ≥2 CRS and no treatment discontinuations at the recommended regimen.

Wholly-Owned R&D Pipeline
On October 24, 2026, Zymeworks presented new Phase 1 data for folate receptor alpha-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, ZW191 , at the ESMO Annual Congress. Updated data presented for ZW191 demonstrates compelling anti-tumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer across folate receptor alpha expression levels: Confirmed objective response rates of 64.5% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose in patients with high-grade serous platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Median duration of response not yet reached at either dose level at median 7 months follow-up, with six-month progression-free survival rate of 61% in both groups. Favorable tolerability profile, particularly at 6.4 mg/kg, supports continued clinical development in partnership or through a strategic collaboration. On November 7, 2026, Zymeworks presented preclinical data at SITC on a novel PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 multispecific antibody with optimized geometry that achieves targeting of IL-7 to PD-1+ T cells. The poster presentation titled “Engineering targeted IL-7 delivery to enhance anti-tumor T cell fitness and persistence” shows that combining checkpoint and angiogenesis blockade with a T cell cytokine signal, PD-1xVEGFxIL-7 represents a mechanistically distinct strategy to improve the durability of anti-tumor responses. On December 13, 2026, Zymeworks will present new preclinical data for a penta-specific antibody at the American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting and Exhibition via a poster presentation titled “ZW1953: A multispecific T cell engager targeting FLT3, CLEC12A, and CD33 with conditional CD28 co-stimulation designed to overcome resistance mechanisms and improve treatment responses in AML”, representing the first scientific disclosure for Zymeworks in a hematological cancer indication.

Financial Results for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026
Financial Results for the Quarter Ended
September 30, 2026
The key financial highlights for our 2026 third quarter results are as follows:
Theravance Biopharma Acquisition – The acquisition of Theravance Biopharma closed on September 23, 2026 and had a limited impact on third quarter operating results given the timing of the transaction. Theravance Biopharma contributed approximately $1.5 million of revenue during the quarter, reflecting seven days of ownership following the acquisition date. The primary earnings impact related to integration and transaction-related costs associated with the acquisition.
Theravance Biopharma Acquisition –
Revenue – Total revenue was $256.5 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $27.6 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to the $250.0 million milestone earned from Jazz following the U.S. approval of Ziihera for first-line HER2-positive GEA in August 2026. The increase was partially offset by the absence of a $25.0 million development milestone from Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine recognized during the third quarter of 2025.
Revenue –
Research and Development (R&D) Expenses – R&D expenses were $36.1 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $35.6 million for the same period in 2025. R&D expenses were generally consistent with the prior year period, as lower spending on ZW171 following discontinuation of the program in 2025 and reduced spending on certain preclinical programs after completion of IND-enabling activities were largely offset by employee-related costs associated with the Theravance Biopharma acquisition.
Research and Development (R&D) Expenses –
Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses – SG&A expenses were $42.7 million in 3Q-2026, compared to $14.1 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by costs associated with the Theravance Biopharma acquisition, including severance and transaction-related professional fees, together with higher stock-based compensation expense associated with 2026 equity awards, including leadership transition awards and the settlement of certain Theravance Biopharma equity awards.
Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses –
Other Income, net – Net other expense was $4.4 million in 3Q-2026, compared to net other income of $3.8 million for the same period in 2025. The change was driven primarily by interest expense related to the royalty-backed note financing arrangement with Royalty Pharma executed in March 2026 and lower interest income resulting from reduced investment balances.
Other Income, net –
Net Loss – Net income was $173.7 million in 3Q-2026, compared to a net loss of $19.6 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was driven primarily by the $250.0 million milestone earned from Jazz following U.S. approval of Ziihera for first-line HER2-positive GEA in August 2026, partially offset by nonrecurring acquisition related costs and interest expense associated with the Company's royalty-based note financing arrangement with Royalty Pharma in March 2026.
Net Loss –
Since initiating its share repurchase program in August 2024, the Company has cumulatively utilized $279.8 million to reacquire 12,940,827 shares at an average price of $21.63 per share (exclusive of commission expense and estimated excise tax). As of November 6, 2026, the Company had approximately 69.0 million common shares outstanding.
About Zymeworks Inc.
Zymeworks is a global biotechnology company building a diversified portfolio of healthcare assets designed to generate durable cash flows while advancing innovative medicines for difficult-to-treat diseases. The Company’s asset and royalty aggregation strategy combines a growing portfolio of commercial and near-commercial assets, including YUPELRI ® (revefenacin), with a differentiated internal research and development engine. Zymeworks’ portfolio also includes Ziihera ® (zanidatamab-hrii), a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody discovered and developed by Zymeworks and commercialized through global partnerships with Jazz Pharmaceuticals and BeOne Medicines, and pasritamig, a clinical-stage multispecific antibody developed by Johnson & Johnson using Zymeworks’ proprietary antibody engineering technologies.
Zymeworks is advancing a diverse pipeline of novel biotherapeutics, leveraging its proprietary Azymetric™ platform and expertise in antibody-drug conjugates, multispecific antibodies and other next-generation antibody technologies. These capabilities, together with Zymeworks’ integrated drug development expertise, enable the Company to develop differentiated therapeutics and create value through both internal innovation and strategic partnerships.
For more information about Zymeworks, its portfolio and pipeline, visit www.zymeworks.com and follow @ZymeworksInc on X.

Accessibility: Skip TopNav Aclaris Therapeutics Announces Top Line Phase 2 Results for its Anti-TSLP Monoclonal Antibody Bosakitug (ATI-045) in Atopic Dermatitis (AD) November 16, 2026 03:28 ET | Source: Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. - The ADMIRATION Trial Did Not Achieve its Primary Endpoint of Percent Change in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) Score from Baseline at Week 24 - - Aclaris Remains Focused on Prioritizing the Development of its Oral Kinase (ITK) Inhibitors and Anti-TSLP/IL-4Rα Bispecific Antibody ATI-052 - WAYNE, Pa., Nov.  16, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: ACRS), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel product candidates for immuno-inflammatory diseases, today announced top line results from the Phase 2 ADMIRATION trial that evaluated the efficacy and safety of bosakitug (ATI-045), a humanized anti-thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) monoclonal antibody, in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. The trial did not achieve the primary or secondary endpoints; however, pharmacodynamic (PD) results showed robust target engagement of TSLP and downregulation of biomarkers related to immune activation including Th1, Th2, and Th17. Bosakitug was generally well tolerated in this trial. “We are disappointed that the ADMIRATION trial did not overcome the historical challenges of addressing atopic dermatitis with an anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody alone,” said Dr. Neal Walker, Chief Executive Officer of Aclaris. “We are grateful to the patients and investigators whose participation and commitment made this study possible.” Dr. Walker continued, “These results do not change our development priorities, which remain focused on our oral kinase inhibitors and anti-TSLP/IL-4Rα bispecific antibody ATI-052. First and foremost, we have initiated the Phase 2b trial of our oral ITK/JAK3 inhibitor modzatinib in lichen planus. We’ve also completed the IND-enabling studies for our oral ITK inhibitor ATI-9494 and expect to file the IND this quarter. Lastly, we intend to initiate the Phase 2b trial with ATI-052 in eosinophilic esophagitis in the first quarter of 2027. We expect to achieve numerous important regulatory, clinical, and data milestones throughout 2027 with each of these assets.” About Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a pipeline of novel product candidates to address the needs of patients with immuno-inflammatory diseases who lack satisfactory treatment options. The company has a multi-stage portfolio of product candidates powered by a robust R&D engine. For additional information, please visit www.aclaristx.com and follow Aclaris on LinkedIn . Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. - Dual Inhibition of ITK and JAK3 Provides Potential for Modzatinib to be the First Mechanistically Complete Oral Therapy for Lichen Planus, an Unaddressed Inflammatory Disease with No Approved Therapeutic Options - - Unique Mechanism Targets Key Pathways Implicated in LP Pathology, T-cell Receptor Signaling Upstream and Effector Cytokine Signaling Downstream - WAYNE, Pa., Nov.  16, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: ACRS), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel product candidates for immuno-inflammatory diseases, today announced initiation of its randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2b A LP HA trial of modzatinib (ATI-2138) in patients with moderate-to-severe lichen planus (LP); the first cohort to be enrolled will be patients with oral erosive lichen planus (OLP). The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted Fast Track Designation for modzatinib for moderate-to-severe LP. LP is a chronic, CD8 cytotoxic T cell-driven inflammatory disease that can cause painful oral erosions, permanent scarring hair loss, and genital lesions, and is associated with a risk of malignancy in oral LP. Modzatinib is a potential first-in-class oral therapy with a unique mechanism that inhibits both ITK and JAK3, potentially addressing LP at multiple points in its immune pathology. ITK inhibition blocks T-cell receptor signaling upstream, reducing T cell activation, CD8 T cell-mediated cytotoxicity, and inflammatory cytokine production, while JAK3 inhibition blocks downstream cytokine signaling to limit T cell proliferation, activation, and survival. “We are excited to initiate the A LP HA trial, particularly given the unmet medical need in lichen planus and the mechanistic potential for modzatinib in this indication,” said Dr. Jesse Hall, Chief Medical Officer of Aclaris. “Modzatinib has demonstrated activity in multiple non-clinical disease models, including severe alopecia areata, vitiligo, and rheumatoid arthritis, as well as in a Phase 2a trial in atopic dermatitis with rapid and sustained improvements across clinical and patient-reported measures of disease severity, pruritus, and quality of life. This provides support for its continued development across immuno-inflammatory diseases. There are no FDA-approved therapies for people living with this debilitating disease, and we believe that modzatinib has the potential to be the first mechanistically complete oral therapy in this setting.” The A LP HA trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2b study to assess the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of modzatinib at two dose levels compared with placebo in approximately 100 participants with biopsy-proven, moderate-to-severe LP not adequately controlled with topical therapies. The trial is designed to include three patient cohorts: oral erosive lichen planus, cutaneous lichen planus (CLP), and lichen planopilaris (LPP). The primary endpoints are change from baseline in activity score of the Oral Disease Severity Score (ODSS) at Week 16 (OLP), modified Lichen Planus Area and Severity Index (LPASI) score at Week 16 (CLP), and Lichen Planopilaris Activity Index (LPPAI) score at Week 24 (LPP). A variety of secondary and exploratory endpoints will also be assessed. Select Upcoming Milestones Modzatinib : Top line results from the OLP cohort are expected in the second half of 2027. ATI-9494 (ITK/TXK inhibitor): Aclaris expects to file the IND this quarter. The planned Phase 1 clinical program will evaluate single (SAD) and multiple ascending doses (MAD) of ATI-9494 followed by a proof-of-concept portion in an undisclosed indication. The Company expects to initiate the trial in the first quarter of 2027. ATI-052 (anti-TSLP/IL-4Rα bispecific antibody): Following the recent positive primary analysis results from Phase 1b proof-of-concept trials (press release here ), Aclaris expects to prioritize the development of this molecule in eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE). The Company intends to initiate the Phase 2b trial of ATI-052 in EoE in the first quarter of 2027. About Modzatinib (ATI-2138) Modzatinib is a highly potent and selective novel investigational pharmacologic agent that acts as a dual inhibitor of interleukin-2-inducible T cell kinase (ITK) and Janus kinase 3 (JAK3). ITK regulates T cell receptor signal transduction and inhibition of this kinase can affect T cell differentiation and activation. JAK3 is a key signal transduction kinase that forms a heterodimer with JAK1, modulates JAK1 phosphorylation of signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 (STAT5), and regulates cytokines that signal through the IL-2Rγ c to affect lymphocyte proliferation and activation. The results observed in preclinical animal models of inflammation and autoimmune diseases, coupled with the favorable safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics profile in healthy human studies and a Phase 2a trial in atopic dermatitis, support the potential for modzatinib to be the first mechanistically complete oral therapy for a variety of immuno-inflammatory disorders. About Lichen Planus Lichen planus (LP) is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory disease that can affect the mucous membranes, genitalia, skin, nails, and scalp. It is estimated to affect approximately 0.1% to 2% of the global population; up to 40% of patients seek treatment despite no FDA-approved targeted therapeutic interventions. Disease management is currently focused on immunosuppression and topical symptom control. When LP affects the mouth, it can cause painful burning sores, and erosive forms can make eating, drinking, and oral hygiene difficult; there is a malignancy concern with OLP. Common symptoms of cutaneous LP include severely itchy, flat-topped bumps or scales that often appear on the wrists, ankles, and lower back. LP can also lead to nail changes, scarring and permanent hair loss (lichen planopilaris), and painful genital lesions. Lichen planus can significantly affect a patient’s quality of life, with symptoms such as chronic itch, pain, and discomfort contributing to sleep disturbance, emotional distress, anxiety, depression, and limitations in daily activities. About Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. Aclaris Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a pipeline of novel product candidates to address the needs of patients with immuno-inflammatory diseases who lack satisfactory treatment options. The company has a multi-stage portfolio of product candidates powered by a robust R&D engine. For additional information, please visit www.aclaristx.com and follow Aclaris on LinkedIn .
